record.original_question: Consider the princess and monster game on the interval [-1,1], where the monster moves continuously with maximum speed 1 and the princess may relocate with unbounded speed. Let M1 be the monster strategy that chooses an arbitrary initial point and direction, runs to one endpoint, and then back to the other endpoint; let M2 be the strategy that again chooses an arbitrary initial point and direction, runs until meeting the sweeper coming from that direction, then turns around, joins that sweeper, and finally traverses to the other endpoint; and let P be the class of princess strategies that either stay at an endpoint or start at a point in [-1+ε,-ε]∪[ε,1-ε], wait until the nearest-end sweeper is ε-close, then run to the middle and back to an endpoint. Is it true that against any mixed strategy supported on M1∪M2 there exists an optimal princess response supported on P, so that the interval game reduces to the stated optimization problem?

evidence.quote: In [ 2] it has been conjectured that an optimal mixed strategy for M can be based upon the following pure strategies: M1 Choose an arbitrary initial point and an arbitrary direction. M runs in that di- rection until the end, and then back until the other end. M2 Again choose an arbitrary initial point and an arbitrary direction. But now M runs until he meets the sweeper coming from that direction, then turns around and runs until the end, joining the sweeper, and then back until the other end.

If the strategy space of the monster is restricted to these pure strategies, then the optimal mixed strategy of the princess is based upon the following pure strategies: P Choose an inﬁnitesimal ε > 0. Either hide at an end-point and remaind immo- bile, or choose an arbitrary initial point in [−1 + ε,−ε]∪[ε,1−ε] and remain

there until the sweeper that st arts from the nearest end point is ε-close. Then run to the the middle until ε-close, turn, and run back until the end. It is possible to show that there exists an optimal response in M1 ∪M2 against any mixed strategy that is based on P. The conjecture in [ 2] is that conversely against any mixed strategy that is based on M1 ∪M2 there exists an optimal response that is in P. If this conjecture is true, then the princess and monster game on an interval reduces to a standard optimization problem that can be solved numer- ically by discretization and linear programming.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Princess-and-Monster pursuit-evasion game played on the closed interval [-1,1]. The Monster moves continuously along the interval with speed at most 1; the Princess may relocate instantaneously to any point (her position is hidden). Neither player observes the other. The payoff to the Monster is the (first) capture time, defined as the first time t ≥ 0 at which the two players occupy the same point; the Monster minimizes and the Princess maximizes the expected capture time.

Define the following pure Monster strategies, parameterized by an initial point x₀ ∈ [-1,1] and a direction d ∈ {-1,+1}:
• M1(x₀,d): start at x₀, move at speed 1 in direction d until reaching the corresponding endpoint, then reverse and traverse to the opposite endpoint.
• M2(x₀,d): start at x₀, move at speed 1 in direction d until meeting the "sweeper" coming from that direction (i.e., a Monster trajectory of type M1 traveling toward the same endpoint), then turn around and join that sweeper to the endpoint in direction d, then reverse and traverse to the opposite endpoint.

Fix an infinitesimal ε > 0 and define the following pure Princess strategies, forming a class P:
• Stay forever at an endpoint -1 or +1.
• Choose an initial point y₀ ∈ [-1+ε, -ε] ∪ [ε, 1-ε], remain stationary until the M1-type sweeper that starts at the endpoint nearest to y₀ is within distance ε of y₀, then run at unbounded speed to the midpoint 0, and finally run back to the endpoint on the same side as y₀.

It is known that, against any mixed Princess strategy supported on P, there exists an optimal Monster response supported on M1 ∪ M2.

Question: Is the converse true? That is, against any mixed Monster strategy supported on M1 ∪ M2, does there exist an optimal Princess response supported on P? Equivalently, does the Princess-and-Monster game on [-1,1] reduce to the finite-dimensional optimization problem (solvable by discretization and linear programming) of finding a saddle point in mixed strategies on (M1 ∪ M2) × P?
artifact.status_search_result: The princess-and-monster game on an interval remains unsolved: while the value on a circle is known, on the interval only bounds (e.g., 15/11 ≤ V ≤ 13/9) are established, and the conjecture that optimal strategies are supported on the described classes M1 ∪ M2 and P (which would reduce the game to a finite linear program) is reported as unproven in subsequent literature including a numerical-approach paper and a 2023 thesis.

status_evidence.title: Princess and monster game - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Only the circle network has been solved; for the interval, only bounds and conjectures are known.
status_evidence.claim: The interval version of the princess-and-monster game remains unsolved.

status_evidence.title: A Numerical Approach to the 'Princess and Monster' Game on an Interval
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical approach via discretization and linear programming based on the conjectured strategy classes.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still treated as an open conjecture supporting numerical investigation.

status_evidence.title: The Princess and Monster Game on the Circle and the Interval (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjectured optimal strategies and unresolved status of the interval game.
status_evidence.claim: Recent thesis confirms the conjecture has not been proved.
